name: Italian fascism
summary: Italian fascism, the original fascist movement and regime under Mussolini, holds that the nation-state is an ethical and spiritual whole to which individuals, classes and private interests are subordinate. It rejects liberal democracy, Marxian socialism and pacifism in favour of one-party rule under a leader, class collaboration through corporations, national expansion and war as a source of vitality, and a revived Roman heritage.
scope: The movement and regime at its peak (1922-1943), centred on Mussolini and Gentile's Doctrine of Fascism (1932), the corporative state, and the Lateran accords and 1938 racial laws. The radical 1919 programme counts only where it stayed in force. Nazi biological racism as a system, later neo-fascist movements and the Salo Republic are excluded.

sources.usedFor: Militia and OVRA, education and youth organisations, welfare and Dopolavoro, Lateran agreements, colonial wars, racial laws, League withdrawal, autarky campaigns.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The regime ran insurance, sick pay and pension schemes for citizens as part of national strength, so a state-guaranteed service is inferred as acceptable, though no universal health system is documented.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages were set and cut by the state and the corporations rather than raised as a social goal, so a substantial rise runs against the documented record.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Doctrine treats the liberal state as a passive non-director, and the regime moved to state direction of the economy from 1925 onward.

public-ownership.rationale: The IRI (1933) brought roughly a fifth of industry under state control, giving Italy among the highest state ownership outside the USSR, though private property stayed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The 1919 programme's capital levy was dropped and the regime in power repealed the inheritance tax and cut taxes in its liberal phase.

unions-good.rationale: Independent unions were replaced by compulsory state-controlled syndicates under the 1926 Rocco laws, so adherents value national syndicates, not free unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private property was kept but subordinated to the state, so it is not an almost inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The state required permission for expansion, mergers and layoffs and coordinated prices and wages with business bodies.

cut-welfare.rationale: The regime built pensions, sick pay, unemployment benefit and the Dopolavoro leisure network, so it expanded rather than cut welfare for citizens.

worker-ownership.rationale: Corporatism kept private ownership; the 1919 demand for proletarian management of industries was never implemented.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The OVRA secret police (1927) and the totalitarian state treat broad surveillance of the population as a normal tool of order.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the regime's stress on moral hygiene and discipline of youth; drugs were not a documented issue.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: the regime censored widely for the state's own ends but not to protect minorities, so adherents would not endorse such a law.

strong-leader.rationale: The Duce held personal dictatorial power above parliament, and the movement's slogan was Believe, Obey, Fight.

state-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state the foundation and source of all value and liberty.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: the regime monopolised armed force in party and state hands and disarmed opponents, though private gun law is not documented in my sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Blackshirt militia (1923) and OVRA (1927) were built up, and military power was glorified as the measure of the nation.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The regime condemned prostitution and pornography as threats to youth's moral hygiene.

decide-locally.rationale: Local elections were abolished in 1926 and the totalitarian state centralised authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the stress on authority and discipline; penal philosophy is not discussed in my sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Women were assigned motherhood and men soldiering, with pronatalist subsidies for larger families.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Homosexuality was condemned as a social disease and persecuted, so legal marriage is rejected.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pronatalism and moral hygiene (contraception condemned) imply opposition to legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: After the 1929 Lateran accords Catholicism became the state religion, and the regime cited Church tradition for its policies.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The regime enforced racial hierarchy in its colonies and from 1938 at home, so it rejects redress for racial groups.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The regime treated women's role as bearing children and men's as soldiering, presenting these as natural duties rather than conventions.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Fascism centres on Romanitas, the Third Rome and cultural nationalism, including forced Italianization of minorities.

gradual-change.rationale: Fascism presented itself as a revolutionary rebirth that rejected nineteenth-century liberal ideology, though it kept the monarchy and Church.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from ethnic nationalism and pronatalism as a substitute for foreign population; Italy was mainly a country of emigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Doctrine denies pacifism and Italy left the League of Nations in 1937 after sanctions.

free-trade.rationale: After 1925 the regime turned to protectionism and from 1934 to autarky.

nation-first.rationale: The Doctrine puts the state and national expansion above internationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: fascism subordinates rights to the state's interest and has no universal human-rights doctrine.

open-borders.rationale: Totalitarian nationalism with Italianization of minorities is incompatible with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Empire growth and autarkic production were goals; the Doctrine treats growth of power as vitality.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from prioritising state power and production over other goals.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the myth of indefinite progress and happiness, though the regime showcased technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from autarky and strategic-industry priorities favouring domestic energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Fascism took power through squadrist violence and the March on Rome and called itself a revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of mass democracy and the corporative technical representation scheme.

central-planning.rationale: The regime used dirigisme and state-business bodies but kept private ownership and profit, short of central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred: markets were tolerated under state direction with private ownership, not worker or public ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Anachronistic single-tax idea; inferred from the regime's tax-cutting and corporatist practice.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The regime repealed the socialist-era inheritance tax in 1922-25.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: welfare was tied to work, family and service to the nation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Business pressure produced protectionism from 1925 and full autarky tariffs after 1934.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The IRI and state-business bodies directed strategic industry and public works.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred from the ruralist wheat and smallholder rhetoric; the regime also protected landowners and large firms.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Doctrine opposes Marxian socialism and the regime retained wages under state-set bargaining.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The state took over bank holdings and required foreign securities to be surrendered to the Bank of Italy.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Employer and worker syndicates linked in corporations set economic policy with the state.

one-party-rule.rationale: The National Fascist Party declared the state totalitarian in 1925 and became the sole legal party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Mussolini accepted the monarchy in 1922 and governed alongside the king while limiting his power.

democracy-best.rationale: The Doctrine rejects rule by numbers through periodic consultation.

direct-votes.rationale: Fascism rejected popular sovereignty; occasional plebiscites were controlled ratifications.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based rule is rejected; the state and corporations stand above classes.

right-to-secede.rationale: The totalitarian nation-state treats national unity as sacred and expands rather than lets go.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Doctrine affirms the immutable and beneficial inequality of mankind.

political-violence-never.rationale: Blackshirt paramilitary violence brought the movement to power and OVRA terror sustained it.

war-builds-character.rationale: War alone raises human energy to its highest tension, according to the Doctrine.

separate-church-state.rationale: Lateran treaty made Catholicism the state religion, and the regime kept a veto over bishops.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law derives from the state, not scripture, though the regime co-operated with the Church.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state absolute and the source of all value, so justice, policing and defence are state monopolies, never market services.

military-superiority.rationale: Armed power and empire were measures of vitality and the regime built up its military.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The regime Italianized South Tyrol and Slavic areas and later enacted racial laws, though its nation was cultural and historical more than purely ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Doctrine denies that class war is the driving force of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The Doctrine praises the immutable, beneficial and fruitful inequality of mankind, so adherents reject levelling of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from colonial conquest and settler policy in Libya and Ethiopia.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from the regime's pride in empire and denial of colonial wrongs.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: fascism prioritises the nation-state and Italian empire over unions of civilizations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates the individual to the state and makes duty central.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The individual has only the margin of liberty the state grants, and duty to the state comes first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred: fascism values nation and state; environment was not a doctrinal topic.

limit-population.rationale: Pronatalism and subsidies for large families were regime policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The regime pursued industrialisation, autarky and showpiece technology.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Futurist currents existed, but the regime stressed order and institutions over disruptive change; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from state control of bodies and morality.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the personal authority of the leader.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a regime built on secret police surveillance (OVRA) that would not accept communications beyond state reach.

restore-past-order.rationale: Fascism claimed a forward-looking national rebirth drawing on Rome rather than a restoration of a lost order; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The regime shifted economic policy through four phases pragmatically, though the Doctrine insists on faith and ideology.

direct-action.rationale: Squadrist violence and the March on Rome were direct action against parliament and the left.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred: violence and coercion were used openly to build a hierarchical state.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The regime glorified modern empire, industry and technology.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Corporatism organised producers into hierarchical, function-specific syndicates and corporations, the opposite of abolishing the division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Doctrine affirms inequality and opposes the materialist socialism behind this idea.

production-for-use.rationale: The regime kept private profit and made corporations profitable under state direction, so production stayed tied to profit and national output goals.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Fascism denies class exploitation as the basis of society and allowed corporations to profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Doctrine denies class struggle as history's engine and rejects Marxian socialism, so class dictatorship is refused in favour of a national state above classes.

collective-farming.rationale: The regime defended landowners and smallholder ideals rather than collectivising.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Doctrine treats war as human nature and national vitality, not as a product of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is the source of all value and its claims on citizens are legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: The state limits liberty by its own aims; individual liberty is a margin it grants.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Doctrine holds that individuals exist only within the state.

conscription.rationale: War and military service are central duties and the regime militarised youth.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit and consent are irrelevant to an absolute state and a loyal nation.

state-as-business.rationale: The Doctrine treats the state as an ethical and spiritual entity with a will of its own, not an enterprise serving customers who may leave.

positive-liberty.rationale: Fascism rejects the materialist premise; liberty is duty within the state.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred: the regime itself controlled schools, textbooks and the press, so adherents would see elected office as weak but would not describe media and academia as a rival power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The 1938 Manifesto of Race and racial laws asserted biologically grounded racial differences.

organic-representation.rationale: A planned chamber of corporations of 22 corporations replaced party representation.

total-state.rationale: The party declared a totalitarian state in 1925 and the Doctrine puts everything within the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Fascism promised national renewal after the mutilated victory and liberal decay.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Empire growth is an essential sign of vitality and decline its opposite.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rested on the state and party, though personal oaths to the Duce existed; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Peasants were tied to production campaigns but not bound to lords; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Gentile's idealism treats thought as action, but the regime claimed truth for its own doctrine.

universal-morality.rationale: The Doctrine grounds morality in the state and nation, not in universal reason.

single-common-good.rationale: Class collaboration and the unified state aim at one national interest above group interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Mussolini's stance fluctuated, and the question is outside the Doctrine; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred from nationalist interest in Italians abroad and irredentism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred: Italian was already the state language; not a topic.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporations were state-supervised hierarchies and strikes were criminalised.

school-vouchers.rationale: The regime controlled schooling and textbooks, so choice among schools is not endorsed; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Public works spending tripled in 1929-34 as a response to the Depression.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates economic motives to the state, and the regime restrained business.

rule-by-example.rationale: The regime relied on law, the Blackshirt militia, the OVRA and propaganda to enforce obedience rather than on the rulers' moral example alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: Fascist expansion and Italianization of minorities deny equal self-determination to other peoples.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic: the UN did not exist, but Italy attacked Ethiopia despite League opposition.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Gentile's Doctrine presents fascism as a religious, anti-positivist conception with the slogan Believe, Obey, Fight.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Pronatalist and welfare benefits were for the national community.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from duty and labour discipline; the regime's benefits were attached to employment.

class-collaboration.rationale: Corporatism aimed at class collaboration instead of conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Fascism celebrated Roman heritage and used it as a national symbol.

dominated-front.rationale: Italy later styled itself a proletarian nation against plutocracies; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: National syndicalism organised workers into national corporations, not as an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Mussolini saw women's main role as bearing children and men's as warriors.

ban-interest.rationale: Banking and credit remained and were state-directed; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Colonial racial segregation followed Libya and Ethiopia and the 1938 racial laws stripped Jews of rights.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the Marxist view of the state, holding it a higher ethical unity that stands above and shapes classes.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: the autarky drive after 1934 favoured maximum domestic production of strategic resources, though oil was not documented in my sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The regime banned minority German and Slavic languages in schools and media and Italianized place names, showing the expectation that others adopt the national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: The regime was pronatalist but this conspiracy theory is anachronistic; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Acerbo law gave two-thirds of seats to the largest party, replacing proportional representation.

national-mission.rationale: The Third Rome idea held that Italy continued Rome's civilizing mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The regime presented male leadership and female motherhood as natural.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Fascism attacked liberal parliamentary politicians; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Fascist demographic policy was pronatalist and Catholic-friendly; coercive eugenics not documented in my sources.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regime's colonial and domestic violence was celebrated or concealed, never accounted for.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Fascism claims a total state directing culture, education and economy, as the party declared in 1925, so a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Colonial rule after Libya and Ethiopia enforced racial segregation, and the 1938 racial laws deepened separation, implying discouragement of mixing.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Doctrine explicitly affirms the immutable inequality of mankind, rejecting equal worth and equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Outside fascist concerns; fascism opposes socialism altogether.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from Italy's own settlement and conquest in Libya and Ethiopia, which adherents defended as civilisation rather than a colonial wrong.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the unitary state, though the Church had its own rights after 1929.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred; Catholic primacy but no documented conversion law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: Italian fascism had no Hindu-style cattle doctrine and no source ties it to such a ban; adherents would not support it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholicism became the state religion and religious teaching is part of the Lateran settlement.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Fascism holds the state grows stronger for national struggle; inferred for a socialist state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Doctrine denies that numbers can govern and places legitimacy in the state.

trade-surplus.rationale: Autarky and import bans aimed at self-sufficiency and reserves.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced Italianization and persecution of minorities; mass transfer is inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Doctrine affirms war and rejects pacifism, and the movement rose by squadrist violence, so initiating force is accepted when serving the nation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Doctrine holds that struggle between peoples drives vitality and history.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The regime outlawed every other party and made the National Fascist Party the sole legal one, justifying it as protecting the state.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The Doctrine grants individuals only the margin of liberty the state allows, with the state an absolute power, so freedom against arbitrary power is not a goal.

separated-powers.rationale: Power was concentrated in the leader and party and parliament was subordinated.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: the party led the whole nation under the Duce rather than the working class, which fascism denied as a revolutionary subject.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Doctrine denies class struggle and subordinates all groups to the nation, so no class has priority on its needs.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred from regime rhetoric favouring ownership and property in a strong family, though council housing was not a documented topic.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and employer lockouts were criminalised under the corporate system, and group stoppages could bring prison sentences.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The regime held population as national strength and subsidised large families, rejecting the claim that numbers cause poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Forced Italianization of minorities shows the regime held national homogeneity to be a condition of strength.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The regime was built on hierarchy and appointment from above, with the Duce naming officials, so selection by chance is foreign to it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The regime relied on the Special Tribunal, OVRA and exceptional measures.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State-business bodies set prices and wages in the 1930s, and the regime accepted direction of prices when scarcity or the national interest required it.

party-controls-media.rationale: The regime controlled press and propaganda through the party and state, as in any totalitarian system.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army stayed loyal to the king, but the MVSN militia was a party force; split inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from ethnic and cultural nationalism that would make citizenship hard to gain.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: hierarchical fascism has no egalitarian rule on officials' pay, and the regime lavished status on leaders.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Discipline, obedience and loyalty to the party line were core.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Doctrine puts the nation-state above everything and Italy left the League of Nations in 1937, so supranational pooling is rejected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Mussolini concentrated power over ministers and the military, though the king formally commanded.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The regime recognised the Catholic hierarchy under the Lateran accords but kept a veto over bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state the supreme authority, and even after the 1929 Lateran accords the regime kept control over bishops' appointments.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war and national loyalty and rejects pacifism, so working for one's own government's defeat is treason.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The regime condemned pornography and enforced moral hygiene.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mussolini ruled without term limits; inferred for presidents.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority runs from the Duce and state downward, and the Doctrine rejects periodic popular consultation, so recall by voters has no place.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Italy sought alliances, later with Germany, and pursued expansion.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not a fascist theme; inferred from property-retaining corporatism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred: the regime kept a regular army and a separate party militia (MVSN) rather than replacing the army with an armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The regime's Battle for Grain and ruralist rhetoric exalted the countryside and farm work, though it also industrialised.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Fascism aimed to complete the unfinished Risorgimento by bringing unredeemed Italian-inhabited lands under Italian rule.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from anti-intellectual strands in squadrist fascism and its preference for action over theory.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Doctrine affirms hierarchy among peoples and empire as vitality.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the repression apparatus; execution policy not detailed in my sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The regime pursued moral hygiene, condemned most contraception and traditional gender roles, so such curricula would be rejected.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred; Gentile's reforms favoured Catholic instruction but not creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The regime condemned pornography, prostitution and homosexuality as part of its moral hygiene campaign for youth.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The nation was defined by shared past and Roman heritage and from 1938 by race, favouring blood ties over birthplace.

minority-language-support.rationale: German and Slavic languages were banned from schools and media.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: the unitary totalitarian state allowed few exemptions, though the Catholic Church had special status after 1929.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Doctrine demands conformity of individuals to the state.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: the regime defended Italy's own financial interests and had no doctrine of international debt relief.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Italy's own nationalists claimed plutocratic powers constrained it; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1919 programme demanded a national assembly to write a constitution, but the regime dropped the demand once in power and ruled by decree and the Acerbo law.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Freedoms were restricted for national goals including autarky and war.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Doctrine's emphasis on national interest and inequality leaves no duty of aid to distant peoples.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's belief in military power and national independence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from rejection of popular consultation, since the Duce was never elected by the people.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state controlled banking and the Bank of Italy served national aims.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Irredentist nationalism, from the claim to unredeemed lands to the Roman heritage, holds historic homelands non-negotiable.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property was retained but made subordinate to the state, which could direct and restrict it for national goals.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Fascism rejected Soviet communism as materialist; this debate is outside its scope.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's priority on production, growth and autarky over caution.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from alliances such as the Pact of Steel with Germany, though the Doctrine mainly stresses national power.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The regime itself annexed Albania in 1939 and Ethiopia and Dodecanese territory, treating conquest as legitimate.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The regime reached accord with the Church in 1929 and gave it special status.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Mussolini led the party as head of government; the king was nominal; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The nation was treated as indivisible and sacred, and the regime used force against its internal opponents and expanded by force abroad.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The unitary totalitarian state allowed no regional distinctiveness.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Duce was exalted by a mass cult but the regime did not claim divine descent for him; Italy kept a monarch.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: tax policy was state-directed and the regime cut taxes only in its early liberal phase.

character-from-environment.rationale: Fascism stressed education of youth but also race and nature; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The state is the source of law and the leader acted by decree.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's love of showpiece technology and empire, but no source ties it to space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Fascism rejected mixed liberal constitutions for a single totalitarian authority.

leader-cult.rationale: The regime was built on mass praise of the Duce, with portraits, slogans and ceremonial devotion as official policy.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from patriarchal family law and the regime's assignment of child-raising to women.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred: the question is internal to Marxism, and fascism denies class struggle in all forms.

land-redistribution.rationale: Landowners and industrialists shaped regime policy, and no large-scale redistribution to farm workers was carried out.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from nationalist and Italianizing policy toward minorities and the regime's own removals.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentist claims covered Dalmatia, Nice, Savoy, Corsica and other Italian-inhabited lands.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: Catholic status after 1929 did not translate into a documented law on leaving religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from moral hygiene and modesty campaigns, though no statute required covering.

common-currency.rationale: Nationalism, autarky and the regime's tight control of the lira and foreign securities reject shared currencies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: fascism pursued an Italian empire rather than union of kindred peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: German and Slavic minority languages were banned from schools and media, and place names Italianized.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred; fascism viewed minorities as threats to the nation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Doctrine explicitly rejects the materialist conception of history and the notion that class war transforms society.

ban-cartels.rationale: The state encouraged business bodies and cartels under corporatism.

no-bailouts.rationale: The IRI was founded in 1933 precisely to rescue failing firms and banks with public money.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: fascism sought to remove liberal limits on the state, but speaks for the nation rather than for majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Public life was male-led and women's role was defined as motherhood.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky was the primary goal from 1934 and after the League sanctions.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the autarkic rejection of international rules, though trade standards were not discussed.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Doctrine says action should be motivated by holiness and heroism, not economics.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Squadristi and the March on Rome created a seizure of power.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The monarchy and the Senate stayed in place, and the regime accepted the king in 1922.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Textbooks were state-controlled from 1929 and stressed national history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial rule in Libya and Ethiopia was justified as Roman civilizing mission.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teachers swore loyalty oaths and Balilla trained pupils for the nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from racial hierarchy: the regime favoured one group, not equal treatment.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the state's takeover of bank holdings and its control of the Bank of Italy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Corporatism claimed to adapt capitalism rather than replace it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Fascism presented modern Italy as heir to ancient Rome, with a Third Rome and Mediterranean ambitions.

delink-world-market.rationale: Autarky for Italy; the statement concerns poor countries; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the idea belongs to Marxist class analysis, which fascism rejects, though it spoke of proletarian nations.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Private choice is subordinate to state aims, and the state imposed racial laws.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Doctrine places no limit on the state, which is absolute; entrenched rights against it are rejected.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Italian nationalists rejected post-1919 settlements; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Duce ruled without competitive election, and the Doctrine rejects rule by numbers through consultation.

minority-veto.rationale: Numbers and individual wills do not bind the state; the state binds individuals.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Obedience to the state and leader is the core duty, and the slogan was Believe, Obey, Fight.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament was reduced to a body picked by the party and then replaced by a chamber of corporations under the Duce.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: not discussed in the sources I opened, and the regime had no animal ethics.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: not discussed in my sources, but the regime saw nature as a resource for the nation.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from corporatist hierarchy and welfare paternalism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Doctrine requires every individual to live within and for the state, so retreat from public life is condemned.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The regime used mass culture and Dopolavoro to mobilise, not pacify; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Fascism claims to rule through unity and force, not in these terms.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the regime's rhetoric that plutocratic nations held back Italy, the proletarian nation.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from ethnic nationalism, though not documented in the sources opened.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: fascist nationalism favours national paths, though the question is internal to socialism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Autarky was the regime's primary goal from 1934, preferring self-sufficiency to foreign trade and capital.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The mutilated victory and unredeemed lands were founding grievances, and the regime later demanded Dalmatia, Nice and Savoy.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from colonial hierarchy in which Italians ruled the subject peoples of Libya and Ethiopia.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascists were the regime's opponents, and the movement opposed liberals, socialists and Giustizia e Libertà.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Fascists embraced totalitarianism but rejected equivalence with communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The ideology has no position on this American historical question, so the answer is neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the regime's cult of national past and its own use of Roman monuments and symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Distinct gender roles but no stated stance on this modern issue.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from a gender-role ideology that treats women as mothers and men as protectors.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The Doctrine says liberal institutions are outworn and fascism fits Italian life.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the regime merged military and party power and glorified soldiers, though the army answered to the king.

paid-care-work.rationale: Subsidies for mothers existed, but women's work was discouraged; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on family and duty, though not a documented topic.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from hierarchy and merit rhetoric, though the regime also gave posts by party loyalty.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Autarky and controls on foreign securities and capital show a wish to keep strategic industries national.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The regime promoted traditional family morality and pronatalism, which treats marriage as a duty rather than a private contract.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Authority runs from the Duce downward, and the Doctrine rejects government by those consulted by number.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State social insurance, pensions and sick pay were expanded under the regime, not privatised.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property was retained, with the state able to direct it, not replaced by use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament became a body picked by the party in 1929 and was later to be replaced by a chamber of corporations, so budget approval by a real elected parliament is not accepted.

single-official-language.rationale: German and Slavic languages were banned from schools and media, and Italian was imposed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from autarky and nationalism, though not documented.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The regime denied equality in principle and enforced racial hierarchy by law, so the statement's premise is rejected.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the myth of happiness and says action should be moved by holiness and heroism instead of economic motive.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from imperial power politics, in which Italy backed separatist groups against rivals, though not documented in my sources.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from imperial power politics, since the regime saw its sphere as Italy's to command.

corporate-influence.rationale: Fascism attacked plutocracy rhetorically, although business shaped policy.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty and autarky, though not a documented topic.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Subsidies that increased with each child were regime policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and economic self-sufficiency, though not documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: the regime ran public works and employment drives during the Depression but no job guarantee is documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democracy and pacifism and holds war as ennobling, so spreading democracy for peace is rejected.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Obedience to the state is the core of the regime's creed, summed up by Believe, Obey, Fight.

non-intervention.rationale: Italy invaded Ethiopia, Albania and other states, treating intervention as a right of strong nations.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: syndicates were organised by branch of production under state control, though not independent unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Antisemitism entered official policy in 1938; before that Mussolini denied it; split so low.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The regime made marriage and family the basis of the nation and gave benefits for children.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Press and propaganda were controlled, and secrecy was normal for the party-state.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: the regime sought national self-sufficiency, not local, though it praised the countryside.

informal-organisation.rationale: Fascism rejected informal groups; it built a hierarchical party and militia.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Italy left the League of Nations and ignored its sanctions, putting national will above international law.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation was defined by Roman heritage, history and later race, not by religion, though Catholicism became the state religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: the idea comes from tributary systems, and Italian fascism sought to be the leading power, not a tributary.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The totalitarian state centralised authority and abolished local elections in 1926.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The regime kept private property including productive property, so it would not endorse common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Doctrine presents fascism as the opposite of Marxian socialism and rejects class war and materialism, so coexistence is not sought.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: the economy mixed state enterprises (IRI) and private firms, though service delivery was not discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: The regime sought the Church's accord and spoke of a religious conception of life.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: fascism claimed to move beyond liberal capitalism and Marxism, though it kept private profit.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The regime held women's role to be motherhood and had no programme of economic transformation for equality.

socialized-care.rationale: The regime held the family to be the foundation of society and pushed women's work toward the home.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from language nationalism and the suppression of minority languages, though not documented in my sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: the regime reworked treaty arrangements as it wished and rejected post-1919 settlements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The totalitarian state allowed no autonomous self-governing communities outside the party and corporations.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Italianization policies in South Tyrol and Slavic areas, which pressed the majority group into them.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Italian fascism presented corporatism as a Third Position between capitalism and Marxism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The regime claimed lands from Roman history and Italian settlement, including Dalmatia and Mediterranean territories.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic for the Italian regime of 1922-43, which ended before the Holocaust was widely known; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: homosexuals were persecuted by confinement and psychiatric measures rather than a formal statute, though the regime condemned it as a social disease.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The one-party state banned other parties and suppressed independent organisations and press.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the Church accord and Catholic state religion, though blasphemy law is not documented in my sources.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Libya and Ethiopia were treated as spaces for Italian settlement and power.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the idea is Islamic doctrine, and fascism opposed anti-colonial resistance.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: not an Italian fascist idea, which put the party-state above religion.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Doctrine rejects democracy and rule by numbers.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The framework assumes egalitarian premises the Doctrine rejects, which affirms inequality and the natural roles of the sexes.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The regime held to fixed sex roles and condemned non-conforming sexuality.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from pronatalism and accord with the Catholic Church.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fascism presented itself as a Third Position beyond both capitalism and Marxism and drew from left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the Marxist critique of capitalist exploitation in favour of class collaboration.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Mussolini ruled Muslims in Libya and courted Islamic opinion in the 1930s while also segregating colonial subjects; adherents were split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Doctrine treats the state as the source of authority and value; the nation, not God or the people, is the source.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: Catholicism was the state religion, so the regime had no program banning religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: workplace harassment was not an issue, and the regime did not regulate it.

social-market-economy.rationale: Corporatism and state direction replaced competition rules and social-market bargaining.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Doctrine repudiates pacifism and exalts war.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: the regime accepted inequality and uneven development, though not as a doctrine on development stages.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Italy joined the Axis through the Pact of Steel and sought alliances for expansion.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The regime accepted the hereditary monarchy of the House of Savoy, though Mussolini was not hereditary.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The regime kept banks and put them under state control rather than turning them into mutual institutions.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: nationalism and autarky would reject outside dictation, though not documented.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: fascism rejected the franchise altogether rather than limiting it by property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The regime defined women by motherhood and rejected feminist critique.

reification.rationale: The statement belongs to Marxist theory, which the Doctrine rejects in favour of spiritual idealism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: the regime put the press under state control and rejected liberal freedoms as such.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: the Duce concentrated lawmaking in his own hands and the party-state, though the regime also issued legal codes.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: from 1938 racial laws stripped Jews of citizenship and professional rights and colonial rule excluded Africans.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic in form, but the Doctrine rejects mass participation in decisions.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the 1938 racial laws restricted marriage with Jews, though sources opened do not detail it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from the 1938 racial laws and exclusion of Jews from economic life, though not detailed in the sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The Doctrine rejects popular consultation and deliberation by lot.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the regime backed Church tradition and cited it for its 1938 laws.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred: fascism attacked plutocracy rhetorically but did not tie it to liberty, which it subordinated to the state.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Homosexuality was condemned as a social disease and the military was a masculine ideal.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Catholicism became the state religion in 1929 and the regime sought Church accord.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The regime built up the Blackshirt militia and OVRA secret police.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The regime enforced a unitary nation-state and Italianized minorities rather than sharing power with them.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The regime expanded state welfare, pensions and leisure organisations rather than leaving aid to charity.

term-limits.rationale: Mussolini ruled without term limits and the Doctrine rejects periodic consultation.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the vote and rule by numbers.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a doctrine that exalts national struggle rather than long-term safety.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from traditional gender roles and accord with the Catholic Church.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The regime held men as heads of family and women as mothers.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nationalism and the abolition of local elections in 1926 make such rights unthinkable.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from state direction of prices, though housing policy was not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Private property was kept and the state favoured national industry, so abolition would be rejected.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Balilla organisation trained youth in uniform for the nation and was a mass regime institution.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's emphasis on military strength.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and sovereignty, though not documented.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: the regime's own colonial killings in Libya and Ethiopia were not acknowledged by it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from productivist rhetoric, although the regime kept private profit.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Doctrine repudiates pacifism and holds that war brings out the highest human energy.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Fascism presented modern Italy as the heir of ancient Rome and the Renaissance, promoting Romanitas.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The regime held sex roles as natural and biological.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The regime assigned women a fixed role as mothers.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Doctrine praises holiness and heroism as motives beyond economics, and the regime honoured its fallen.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Gentile's Doctrine calls fascism a religious conception of life, but it does not cast politics as good against evil; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: irredentism sought to bring Italians into the state, not to treat the homeland as a centre for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state the source of all value, so state building comes first.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from accord with Catholic tradition.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the 1938 racial laws that excluded Jews from professions, though not detailed in my sources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from irredentism, which sought to unite Italian-inhabited lands under one state.

independent-unions.rationale: Independent unions were replaced by compulsory state-controlled labour organisations whose leaders were appointed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: the idea belongs to socialist debates, and fascism rejects socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the regime's state enterprises, but local utilities were not detailed.

second-chamber.rationale: The Senate was not abolished, contrary to the 1919 programme, and remained alongside the Chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: The regime kept private ownership and centralised control, with no municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The totalitarian state centralised authority and abolished local elections.

family-wage.rationale: The regime gave family subsidies that grew with each child and favoured male earners.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The ideology has no stake in drug approval regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from state funding of showpiece science, though not documented.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The regime required citizens to hand foreign securities to the Bank of Italy, and the OVRA monitored society.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a surveillance state that rejected anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: The Doctrine places the state above the individual, whose liberty is a margin the state grants.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Doctrine rejects materialism and calls fascism a spiritual and religious conception of life.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Centralised authority and the abolition of local elections mean no region has secure powers.

gm-crops.rationale: The ideology has no position on this issue; it is anachronistic.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the regime's ruralist rhetoric and measures against urban migration.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: the 1938 racial laws put racial interest above others, though fascism centred on the nation.

racial-pride.rationale: The 1938 Manifesto of Race and racial laws established racial pride as official policy.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Doctrine rejects pacifism and says empire growth is a sign of vitality.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: irredentism sought lands where Italian was spoken, though history and Rome mattered too.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Doctrine rejects the vote and rule by numbers, so communal voting rolls are foreign to it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from the rhetoric of plutocratic powers hemming in Italy after the mutilated victory.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred: university teachers had to join the Fascist Party from 1933, so education was a tool of the state, not a free public good.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from priority on production.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the idea that the nation outlasts its members, though ecological duty was not discussed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the regime saw women as mothers, though not as bringing distinct values to public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Doctrine repudiates pacifism and the regime built up military power.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources suggests the regime sought open diplomacy, and it pursued alliances such as the Pact of Steel as power politics.

capital-controls.rationale: After the League sanctions in 1935 the regime required citizens to surrender foreign securities to the Bank of Italy.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The regime disarmed opponents and moved armed power into state and party hands, with the MVSN as a party militia.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Doctrine glorifies war and demands obedience.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: collective labour contracts were set through state-controlled syndicates, not free bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the regime's welfare approach, though not documented.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Public works spending tripled in 1929-34 and the regime did not accept legal limits on the state.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the rhetoric of Italy as a proletarian nation against plutocracies.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state the highest value, to be strengthened and not smashed.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The regime imposed a single state-directed corporatist order on all communities.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from priority on production.

sacred-nation.rationale: Gentile's Doctrine presents the nation-state as an ethical and spiritual entity that outlasts and gives meaning to its members.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The regime held a unitary national state, denying regional exploitation claims.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: the Doctrine affirms inequality of mankind and a project of remaking the Italian people.

public-service-media.rationale: The press and radio were controlled by the regime rather than free of government.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from Catholic status as state religion and Christian exclusivism.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Battle for Grain and state involvement in agriculture supported wheat production.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's pursuit of military power.

workers-own-party.rationale: The regime had a single party and banned independent organisations.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: the topic was not documented in the regime, and its general moral hygiene approach would favour a ban.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred: not documented, although the regime defined women's role in the family.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The ideology has no position on this question of naming regional languages.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from state direction over property and not a topic of the regime.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: colonial rule treated subject peoples as ruled directly by the Italian state.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: liberty is subordinate to the state's aims in general, though not to the environment specifically.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the regime's law-and-order approach and its heavy reliance on repression.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The regime imposed Italian on minorities and banned other languages in schools.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Compulsory state syndicates replaced independent unions, and membership in them was mandatory.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: the regime held no free elections and had plebiscites controlled by the party.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Catholicism became the state religion under the 1929 Lateran agreements.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Doctrine rejects rule by numbers through periodic consultation as the test of government.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's control of press and radio.

premarital-sex.rationale: The regime pursued moral hygiene and condemned practices outside marriage for the sake of the family.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the regime's own welfare approach tied to work and family.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women got local voting in 1925, but local elections were abolished in 1926, and the regime assigned women to motherhood.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The regime reached accord with the Church and held motherhood as women's role.

race-social-construct.rationale: The 1938 Manifesto of Race presented race as a biological reality.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The regime defined distinct roles for men and women.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The state directed property and could override claims for national ends.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The regime rejected the League and international constraints on the state's sovereignty.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the regime accepted Catholic tradition but the Doctrine does not adopt literal scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from traditional gender roles and denial of local self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: fascism opposed communism and would not defend a communist planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: The regime replaced elections with a party-selected parliament and a chamber of corporations.

national-church-status.rationale: Catholicism became the state religion under the 1929 Lateran treaty.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The regime banned minority languages and Italianized place names in South Tyrol and Slavic areas.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The regime claimed territory by history and conquest, not by votes of inhabitants.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: Italy sought revision of borders and its own colonial expansion.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the regime pursued national power and showpiece production rather than simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: Italy promoted its own settlement in Libya and Ethiopia.

equal-conscription.rationale: The regime held that men are warriors and women mothers.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Fascism's Romanitas and the cult of Italy's soil gave the homeland a spiritual character.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: squadrist killings and the regime's violence went outside the law, though drug policy was not a topic.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's own alliances.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Irredentism and claims for Italians outside the borders led the regime to support such populations.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Private property was kept and the state could direct resources for national ends, not common ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates the individual to the state and denies individual rights as primary.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: tax policy was state-directed and no source ties the regime to consumption tax cuts.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: the regime's benefits were broad national schemes for workers and families.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the regime banned parties and put the leader above them, but it also built corporations as groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Business leaders pushed for protectionism and subsidies, which the regime granted, shaping corporatism to their interests.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the regime banned all parties other than its own and would not tolerate politics organised along any other line.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Fascism combined a sense of shared national past with a commitment to modernization.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The regime promoted traditional family morality and patriarchal authority.

national-resource-control.rationale: Autarky and state direction of strategic industry placed resources under national control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Fascism held that property and wealth serve the nation, so the state may direct them whatever the process behind them.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The radical 1919 manifesto called for a heavy levy on capital, though the regime later dropped it, so a financial tax is inferred only.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The regime did not address the question in this form and its 1938 racial laws cut against any simple reading.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism puts the state above the individual as the source of all right, so law gets authority from the state, not from justice outside it.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the cult of work as national duty; the regime did not address automation directly.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of national expansion and rejection of perpetual peace, which looks to Italian power over a balance among equals.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: corporatism treats labour and capital as partners in production, not labour as the sole source of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Fascism joined national devotion with a politics of the producers, with workers bound into the nation through corporations.

material-over-identity.rationale: The doctrine ranks the nation and its spiritual identity above class and material interest, and rejects Marxian materialism.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Fascism opposed communism and socialism and put all parties but its own down, so it would reject communist-led economic planning.

notes: The regime changed course over time: liberal economics in 1922-25, corporatism and state ownership after 1929, autarky from 1934, and official antisemitism from 1938. The Doctrine excerpt does not cover the family, corporations or race, so those answers rest on reference sources. Several modern questions are answered by inference and marked low.
